headline: Reported incidents in Los Angeles fell 38.8% in the last 12 full months, and 77th Street changed the most among areas.

metrics.label: Incidents analyzed
metrics.explanation: Reported incidents left after cleaning, across all months and areas.

metrics.label: Incidents in Nov 2024
metrics.explanation: Count in the latest full month. That is -8.2% compared with the month before.

metrics.label: Last 12 months vs the 12 before
metrics.explanation: The city logged 142,422 incidents in the last 12 full months and 232,829 in the 12 months before.

metrics.label: Unusual spikes flagged
metrics.explanation: Months where an area, crime type or the whole city ran well above its usual level of the prior 12 months.

metrics.label: Biggest area change
metrics.explanation: The area whose 12-month count moved the most, in either direction, compared with the 12 months before.

findings.statement: Citywide incidents changed -38.8% over the last 12 full months compared with the 12 months before.
findings.evidence: 142,422 incidents in the last 12 months against 232,829 in the 12 months before.
findings.so_what: Use this as the baseline for planning. Judge each area against the citywide direction, not in isolation.

findings.statement: Foothill moved up the most and 77th Street moved down the most over the last 12 months.
findings.so_what: Look first at Foothill when deciding where to add resources. Study what is working in 77th Street.

findings.statement: TRESPASSING moved up the most and BATTERY - SIMPLE ASSAULT moved down the most among crime types.
findings.so_what: Point prevention work at the crime types with the biggest increases, since they add the most new cases.

findings.statement: Spikes are rare but real. The largest was THEFT OF IDENTITY in Mar 2022.
findings.evidence: THEFT OF IDENTITY had 1,820 incidents against a usual 1042. Flagged months: 7 area-months, 41 crime-type-months, 0 whole-city months.
findings.so_what: Review the flagged months first. Check whether a real event, a change in reporting or a data entry batch caused each jump.

findings.statement: In Nov 2024, the biggest month-to-month moves were in Central and TRESPASSING.
findings.evidence: Central: -115 incidents versus the month before. TRESPASSING: -231 incidents.
findings.so_what: Treat one month as a prompt to look closer, not as proof of a trend. Check the next month before changing plans.

method_notes.why: The raw file has one row per incident. Counting rows by month, area and crime type turns it into small tables a dashboard can read quickly.
method_notes.alternative: A database could do the same counts. It adds setup work and is not needed for one file.

method_notes.why: Each area gets a map point (the median of its incident coordinates) and a 12-month change, so the client can see where counts move.
method_notes.alternative: Drawing area boundaries would be more exact, but the data has no boundary file and only point coordinates.

method_notes.method: Anomaly detection with a trailing baseline
method_notes.why: A month is flagged when it is at least 3 standard deviations above the average of the prior 12 months, and also 20+ incidents and 20%+ above it. This is simple to explain and ignores tiny counts.
method_notes.alternative: Forecasting models such as seasonal models could handle seasons better. They are harder to explain and need more tuning for little gain here.

caveats: These are reported incidents, not all crime. Changes can come from reporting habits as well as real changes in crime.
Counts are by the date the incident happened. Recent months may be incomplete if incidents are reported late.
The data has no population figures, so counts are not rates per resident. Larger areas will have more incidents.
The data only has area names, not finer neighborhood names, so 'neighborhood' here means the named area.
2,240 rows had a coordinate of 0. They are counted but have no place on the map.
0 repeated record numbers were removed. 4,697 rows from partly covered months were left out.
Some crime type descriptions are cut off in the source file, so a few names look shortened.
A spike flag needs 12 earlier months, so no flags exist before Jan 2021.
The data shows what changed, not why. Causes need local knowledge.
